name: One Inc.
desc:
Customer Service Representative I | $21/hr | Inbound, No Sales Expectations
Company: One Inc
Industry: Insurance Payments Technology
What Your Day Will Look Like:
 You'd be helping insurance customers, adjusters, and service providers with questions about claim payments processed through One Inc's platform. That means answering questions across phone, email, and chat, walking people through basic troubleshooting or account setup, and calming things down if a customer is upset, looping in a team lead when something needs to go further. You'd keep detailed records of every interaction and share feedback on how the support process could run smoother. It's steady, people-focused work at a company that's essentially the payment engine behind hundreds of insurance carriers.
assessment: Expect a basic assessment, a typing test, and a home internet speed test, since the posting doesn't state otherwise.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
 Education Minimum: Associate degree preferred, or 2+ years of relevant experience
Required Experience: Call center experience and proven remote work experience
Preferred Experience: Insurance experience, payments experience
Required Skills:
Good computer skills, with Word, Excel, and Outlook experience preferred
Excellent customer service and people skills
Strong organizational skills and ability to prioritize quickly
Excellent written and verbal communication
Detail oriented with the ability to follow instructions accurately
Composure under pressure, described as not easily flustered
Best Fit
 This role is ideal for:
Someone with an Associate degree or 2+ years of relevant work experience, plus call center and remote work background
Someone naturally empathetic who enjoys walking customers through troubleshooting
Someone detail oriented who keeps accurate records of every interaction
Someone with insurance or payments experience looking to apply that background in a new setting
Not a Good Fit for
Anyone without an Associate degree or 2+ years of relevant experience, this is a real requirement despite the "entry level" label
Anyone without prior call center or proven remote work experience
Anyone who cannot occasionally work evenings or weekends to support business needs
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
Customer service
Claims payments
Insurance industry
Call center experience
Remote work experience
De-escalation
Multi-channel support (phone, email, chat)
Payments processing
Record keeping
Problem resolution
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
Application
Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you
If the assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen
If the phone screen passes, expect a final interview
Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3 to 15 days on average.
4-5 interview questions for this role:
Tell us about your call center and remote work experience.
Walk us through how you'd help a customer who is upset about a delayed claim payment.
What's your experience, if any, with insurance or payments processing?
How do you stay organized and accurate while documenting customer interactions across multiple channels?
This role occasionally requires evening or weekend work, how do you feel about that flexibility?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
Pay: $21 per hour
Shift: Full-time, 11:00 AM to 8:00 PM Eastern Time (converted to 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM CST)
Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) plan, and a strong commitment to work-life balance
Equipment Provided: Not specified in the posting, and no internet requirement is listed either. Confirm both during the recruiter screen
Felony Friendly?: Not stated. Employment is contingent on successful completion of background screening, and periodic background checks may occur during employment
Drug Test: Not stated
Notes: This is a strong opportunity for a participant who already has some call center and remote work background, especially anyone with insurance or payments experience to bring to the table. The pay is solid at $21 per hour, and the company's scale, over $120 billion in annual payment volume across 300+ carriers, speaks to real stability. Set expectations that this leans more experienced than a true first job despite the "entry level" label in the posting.
Career Pathway: Customer Service Representative I → Customer Service Representative II → Team Lead or Claims Payments Specialist
